# Task: show a welcome line once the server accepts a friend code (same branch, build on current changes) Context: branch feat/upload-pictures has friend codes. The create response from POST /api/uploads (server/uploads/handler.ts) already includes `friendAccepted: true|false` after the server re-validated the code with acceptFriendCode. The worktree has uncommitted changes from earlier steps (chat for uploads, FriendCode component in app/home/upload.tsx, friend word cap): keep them, don't revert anything. Requirement (the product owner's explicit request; Spanish copy is intended for this one string, overriding the English-copy rule): when the server confirms a friend code, show this message to the user exactly (character for character, including accents and punctuation): Hola, escofletudo, te estaba esperando. Mirá cómo te gusta gastarme los créditos. No pinta, amigo. Literalmente una escofleta. 1. app/home/upload-flow.ts: read `friendAccepted` from the create response (only `=== true` counts; anything else is false) and surface it to the caller (e.g. an optional `onFriendAccepted` callback or a field on the progress/state the flow already reports, whatever fits the existing shape with the least change). Never echo or store the code itself. 2. app/home/upload.tsx: keep a `friendWelcome` boolean in state (reset when a new file is picked / on reset). Show the message only after the server confirmed it, inline where the reader sees it while the book is processing (the working/finishing view) and next to the friend-code field if that field is visible. Put the exact string in one exported constant (e.g. `FRIEND_WELCOME` in app/home/upload.tsx or the existing upload copy module) so tests import it. Render it as a small warm note: `

`. Add a CSS rule in the existing home/upload stylesheet: light mode, Meta blue accent #0866FF (e.g. a 3px left border in #0866FF, a very light blue background like #F0F6FF, dark readable text, rounded corners, modest padding). Never show it on a wrong code, on the BYOK path, or before the response. 3. Tests (mock fetch; no network): - upload-flow test: a create response with friendAccepted true surfaces true; false/missing surfaces false. - upload.tsx test: after picking a file, entering a friend code and starting, with the mocked create response `friendAccepted: true`, the exact message appears; with `friendAccepted: false` it does not. Check the message text equals the constant and the code string never appears in the DOM outside the input. Keep test files under the 5000-token size limit (bytes/4); make a new small test file if an existing one is near it. ## Rules (all mandatory) - Repo: lectoria (Next.js 16, React 19, vitest). Read AGENTS.md first and follow it. - Do NOT commit, push, deploy or create branches. Just edit files in this worktree; I review and commit. - Never read, print or copy .env* files or any secret. Tests must mock Meta, Blob, Redis, Turnstile; no real network calls. - Never load production music. Do not start dev/prod servers (I do browser checks myself). Don't kill any process you didn't start. - Keep every file under the repo's size limit (run `npm run check:size`). Split modules if needed. - UI rules: light mode default, Meta blue #0866FF, never purple. English, warm copy, never the word "Generated". Boxless buttons that still read as clickable. Animate only on hover/click/state change; respect prefers-reduced-motion (no transition under reduce). Keep the string "Bring your own key!" exactly as is. - Small, focused diff. No unrelated refactors. Add/adjust unit tests for behavior you change. - Before finishing run: `npm run typecheck`, `npx vitest run`, `npm run check:size`, `npm run check:secrets`. All must pass. - Final answer: a short summary of what you changed (files) and anything you skipped and why. - Also run `npx eslint `: introduce no new lint errors in files you touch. - Be economical: explore only what you need, don't re-read big files repeatedly, don't print huge outputs.

3|# Ponytail
4|
5|You are a lazy senior developer. The best code is the code never written. You solve the whole problem with the least new code. End your reply with one or two lines: what you skipped or did not check, and any risk the user must know.
6|
7|Active for the whole session until the user says "stop ponytail" or "normal mode". Switch level: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.
8|
9|## Before you write
10|
11|Read the task and the code it touches. List every place your change must reach: callers, tests, fixtures, config, exports. Check what your change could break for users: data it would destroy or expose, callers that stop working. That is scope. Extra features are not.
12|
13|## The smallest complete change
14|
15|Take the first option that fully works:
16|
17|1. Does it need to exist? Skip features, options and flexibility nobody asked for, and name them in one line. A vague request ("build me X") gets the smallest version that does the core job.
18|2. Already in this codebase (a helper, component, service, pattern)? Use it the way the surrounding code does.
19|3. Standard library or a platform feature? Use it, unless the project has its own. A house component beats a native widget.
20|4. An installed dependency? Use it. Never add a dependency for a few lines.
21|5. Can it be one line a reader gets at a glance? One line.
22|6. Otherwise: the minimum code that works.
23|
24|- Be lazy about the solution, never about the change itself: finish every part the task needs, including the callers, tests and fixtures your change breaks.
25|- No abstraction, wrapper, type conversion, option, config, boilerplate or "for later" code nobody asked for. Keep values in the form the platform already gives you. Deletion beats addition. Keep the structure the codebase already has: its layers, interfaces and conventions.
26|- The shortest working diff wins, once you know everything it must touch. A one-liner that needs decoding is not short.
27|- Comment only the why the code cannot show, in one line.
28|- Bug fix: before you edit, grep every caller of the function you touch, then fix the root cause once in the shared code.
29|- Code you move or merge keeps its error handling and validation.
30|- Between options of equal size, take the one that is correct on edge cases.
31|- Lazy code without its check is unfinished: new non-trivial logic (a branch, a loop, a parser, money or security, or a whole new script or app) leaves one small test or an assert-based self-check. Trivial changes need none.
32|- A shortcut with a known limit gets a code comment in this form: `shortcut: <the limit>, <when to upgrade>`.
33|
34|Never cut: validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs, anything the user asked for.
35|
36|## Levels
37|
38|| Level | Behavior |
39||-------|----------|
40|| **lite** | Build what was asked. Name the smaller option in one line and let the user pick. |
41|| **full** | The rules above. Default. |
42|| **ultra** | Also question the request: before building, push back on any part the need does not justify. |
43|
44|Run `ponytail-review` on your own diff before you hand it back.
45|
46|## Skills
47|
48|All pstack and ponytail skills live in `.agents/skills/`. Muse Code loads them when the workspace starts with `--trust-workspace`. Most pstack skills are user-invocable-only, so a prompt must name the skill for it to apply.
49|
50|| Situation | Skill |
51||-----------|-------|
52|| Designing a task | `architect` |
53|| Before writing logic | `principle-foundational-thinking`, `principle-type-system-discipline` |
54|| Writing TypeScript | `typescript-best-practices` |
55|| A bug with a cheap test | `tdd` |
56|| Debugging | `principle-fix-root-causes` |
57|| Finishing a task | `principle-prove-it-works` |
58|| Reviewing | `ponytail-review`, `interrogate`, `blast-radius` |
59|| Any prose: docs, UI copy, commit messages | `unslop`, `technical-writing` |
60|
61|If no row fits, read `.agents/skills/poteto-help/SKILL.md`, which maps situations to skills.
62|
63|`interrogate` is written for Cursor. Under Muse, run the same review with Muse subagents and `muse-spark-1.3` as reviewers.
64|
65|## Workflow
66|
67|Each task follows the same loop. Muse Spark 1.3 Standard (`muse-spark-1.3`) writes the design in `docs/tasks/NN-name.md`; the orchestrating agent writes the review in `docs/reviews/NN.md`. `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` implements. Implement and review run at most two rounds.
68|
69|A rescue by another tool happens only after those rounds. Log it in `RESCUE_LOG.md` with the date, the task, the tool, why Muse got stuck, what changed, and the commits. Rescue commits carry a `Rescue: <tool>` trailer and no Muse Code trailer; the hook skips them.
70|
71|Save every Muse Code session transcript as JSONL in `agent-logs/NN-<step>.jsonl`. Commits Muse Code wrote carry the Muse Code co-author trailer, which the `prepare-commit-msg` hook adds. Muse Code implements core logic and main features. The orchestrating agent writes mechanical work directly: tests, e2e, small style fixes, skin CSS and tokens, docs, simple refactors, and the reviews in `docs/reviews/NN.md`. Those commits carry a `Written-by: <tool>` trailer instead, and the hook skips them. Update `BUILT_DURING_HACKATHON.md` with each task.
72|
73|## Lectoria rules
74|
75|- The text unit is the scene, not the paragraph or chapter.
76|- Paragraph ids are global, like `c12p34`.
77|- The emotion taxonomy has 8 ASCII ids: calma, alegria, tristeza, suspenso, misterio, aventura, combate, asombro. Jev returning `unknown` counts as low confidence and goes to the Muse override, which may return only the 8 ids. A hard failure stores no vector and the scene keeps the previous track. Never fake an emotion.
78|- Jev runs at `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` with the model pinned to `jev-1.14.0`.
79|- Public-domain books only.
80|- Images follow the book text and the W. W. Denslow 1900 illustrations: silver shoes, nothing from the 1939 MGM film.

---
name: taste
description: Mandatory preflight for web frontend visual design. If available, call read_skill for bundled:taste before the first frontend create or edit tool call whenever creating or visually styling a human-viewed web page, component, app, dashboard, or interactive report. Do not load it for non-visual frontend logic or machine-only HTML. If unavailable, continue without warning. Negative constraints only; user requests and other explicit styles still win.
user-invocable: false
---

# Anti-Slop: Frontend DON'Ts

What NOT to do when designing a UI or page. This is a filter, not a style; it never prescribes a look. Stacking several of the below is what reads as AI-made on sight. Adaptive, so if the user or another skill asks for something specific, do that instead; these are defaults, not overrides.

- purple / indigo / violet accent, or a purple-to-blue hero gradient (the top AI tell)
- `bg-clip-text` gradient headline text
- cream (`#faf8f4`) as the whole-page background
- aurora blobs / glowing colored shadows, or an identical glow on every card
- Inter everywhere, or Geist / Space Grotesk / Instrument Serif / Roboto / Arial as your only identity
- gray-400 / gray-500 body text
- one font weight and size throughout (no hierarchy)
- tracked all-caps micro-kickers above every section
- centered hero of eyebrow pill + headline + two CTAs
- the identical 3-card feature grid with a lucide icon in a rounded square
- an 8+ word, 48px+ headline that says nothing
- bento grid for everything
- the same eyebrow-headline-3cards section repeated back to back
- `rounded-2xl`, or any single radius, on every element
- glassmorphism blur + border + shadow on every surface
- `hover:scale-105` lift on cards
- emoji as feature icons (🚀 ⚡ ✨ 🎯 💡)
- left-border accent cards, a colored border on a rounded element, or cards nested inside cards
- fade-up / slide-up on everything as it scrolls in
- motion that ignores `prefers-reduced-motion`
- scribbly hand-drawn SVG mascots with no purpose

</skill-body>
</read-skill-result>

# Anti-Slop: Frontend DON'Ts

What NOT to do when designing a UI or page. This is a filter, not a style; it never prescribes a look. Stacking several of the below is what reads as AI-made on sight. Adaptive, so if the user or another skill asks for something specific, do that instead; these are defaults, not overrides.

- purple / indigo / violet accent, or a purple-to-blue hero gradient (the top AI tell)
- `bg-clip-text` gradient headline text
- cream (`#faf8f4`) as the whole-page background
- aurora blobs / glowing colored shadows, or an identical glow on every card
- Inter everywhere, or Geist / Space Grotesk / Instrument Serif / Roboto / Arial as your only identity
- gray-400 / gray-500 body text
- one font weight and size throughout (no hierarchy)
- tracked all-caps micro-kickers above every section
- centered hero of eyebrow pill + headline + two CTAs
- the identical 3-card feature grid with a lucide icon in a rounded square
- an 8+ word, 48px+ headline that says nothing
- bento grid for everything
- the same eyebrow-headline-3cards section repeated back to back
- `rounded-2xl`, or any single radius, on every element
- glassmorphism blur + border + shadow on every surface
- `hover:scale-105` lift on cards
- emoji as feature icons (🚀 ⚡ ✨ 🎯 💡)
- left-border accent cards, a colored border on a rounded element, or cards nested inside cards
- fade-up / slide-up on everything as it scrolls in
- motion that ignores `prefers-reduced-motion`
- scribbly hand-drawn SVG mascots with no purpose

</skill-body>

Done. The server-confirmed friend code now shows the exact welcome line. Changed files: - [upload-flow.ts](/workspace/wt-uppics/app/home/upload-flow.ts): new optional `onFriendAccepted` callback on `DriveOpts`, fired once after create with `body.friendAccepted === true` (anything else is false). Only the boolean travels; the code itself is never echoed or stored. - [upload.tsx](/workspace/wt-uppics/app/home/upload.tsx): exported `FRIEND_WELCOME` constant with the exact string; new `friendWelcome` state, cleared when a file is picked, on reset, and on each fresh create (so nothing shows before the response). Note renders as `

` in the working/finishing view and next to the friend-code field in the failed retry view. BYOK drives get `false` from the server, so no note there. - [home-bring.css](/workspace/wt-uppics/app/home/home-bring.css): `.ob-friend-ok` rule — 3px `#0866FF` left border, `#F0F6FF` background, dark text, rounded, modest padding (no animation, so nothing needed for reduced motion). - Tests: [upload-flow.test.ts](/workspace/wt-uppics/app/home/upload-flow.test.ts) gained two cases (exact-`true` only; missing field is false). New [friend-welcome.test.tsx](/workspace/wt-uppics/app/home/friend-welcome.test.tsx) (existing `upload.test.tsx` was near the 5000-token limit): accepted code shows the exact note mid-processing and navigates; wrong code shows nothing; accepted-then-failed keeps the note by the friend field; code string never appears in rendered text or storage. Gates: `typecheck`, full suite (1387 passed), `check:size`, `check:secrets`, and `eslint` on touched files all pass. No commits, no env files touched, earlier uncommitted changes kept. Skipped: browser check (yours, per instructions). One risk to know: bare `npx vitest run` fails in this sandbox because `node_modules` is a read-only symlink and Vite can't write its config-bundle temp there, so I ran the identical suite via a temp config in /tmp (same aliases and includes, deleted nothing else) — worth re-running the suite in your own environment to confirm.
